summary: Quarterly partnership review focused on dramatic usage growth in Feb, a reliability incident on 2026-02-18, rightsizing opportunities to reduce cost, and timeline for private deployment evaluation. Agreement to run a 2-week pilot and share security artifacts ahead of renewal discussion.
transcript:
[00:00] Alexis Kim: All right everyone thanks for hopping on. This is Alexis at Redwood. Quick roll call?
[00:07] Maya Patel: Maya here - Head of AI at Stratus Therapeutics. Hey.
[00:10] Jordan Lee: Jordan, platform. Morning.
[00:12] Samuel Ortiz: Sam, CTO.
[00:14] Elena Park: Elena from security.
[00:15] Diego Martinez: Diego, customer success, Redwood.
[00:18] Priya Nair: Priya, solutions engineering. I'll go through the infra bits.
[00:21] Alexis Kim: Great. Agenda - usage and cost trends, reliability postmortem, recommendations for rightsizing, private deployment timing, next steps for renewal. Anything to add?
[00:31] Maya Patel: No that covers it. We're mainly worried about the cost spike in Feb and the outage last week.
[00:35] Alexis Kim: OK let's jump in. Diego - can you run the numbers first?
[00:39] Diego Martinez: Yeah sure. So quick snapshot - last 90 days tokens have increased 2.8x, but spend is 4.1x due to high tail latency causing more retries and some large batched jobs hitting full context. There's a breakout spreadsheet I'll share after the call. The big drivers were experimental batch jobs and a ramp of inference for our pharmacovigilance assistant.
[01:05] Jordan Lee: We did push a couple of bulk scoring jobs - those were mis-scheduled during peak periods, my bad.
[01:11] Alexis Kim: No worries. Did those use the streaming endpoints or standard generation?
[01:15] Jordan Lee: Standard gen, long sequence lengths - average seq length jumped to 1,800 for those runs.
[01:20] Priya Nair: And for context that length touches model selection and kernel paths - costs multiply non-linearly with sequence length. Also our autoscale config didn't favor dedicated burst, so they hit hosted pools and paid premium.
[01:33] Maya Patel: Is that because we have burst disabled? We thought burst would only be for dedicated.
[01:37] Priya Nair: There's a policy mix - for your org the route was set to hosted for cost control but during peak it didn't fallback to dedicated because the config requires explicit allow for burst. It's a bit of a mismatch.
[01:49] Samuel Ortiz: So is the fix to change routing to allow dedicated burst or to change batching/queueing? Which is lower risk?
[01:56] Priya Nair: Low risk path is rightsizing and input batching — re-schedule bulk jobs to off-peak and use the continuous batching config. Higher predictability is reserving dedicated capacity for the heavy scoring jobs - that costs more upfront but flattens per-token spend.
[02:12] Diego Martinez: We'll propose a mixed approach in the cost breakout - suggested instance mix with a small dedicated pool for long sequences and hosted for ad-hoc queries.
[02:20] Maya Patel: OK. Next - can we talk about the outage on Feb 18 - that caused 2 hours of increased 500s for us.
[02:27] Alexis Kim: Priya lead on the postmortem please.
[02:29] Priya Nair: Yep. Root cause: an autoscaler bug under a particular scheduling pattern plus a cascade from a third-party kernel update on the GPU drivers. TLDR - autoscaler failed to rehydrate KV caches quickly and cold starts spiked latency. We saw retries and client-side re-attempts that amplified load.
[02:48] Elena Park: Did you find any customer data exposure? Security needs to know.
[02:51] Priya Nair: No evidence of data exposure. Logs show request failures and increased latencies but no abnormal access patterns. We'll include the log snippets in the artifact bundle.
[03:01] Diego Martinez: Action we already took - we rolled back the driver change, patched the autoscaler logic, and added a circuit breaker to prevent client-side retry storms. We pushed a canary test to validate the fix.
[03:13] Jordan Lee: We did notice some incorrect entity names in the response during the outage - could be model hallucination amplified by truncated contexts.
[03:20] Priya Nair: That sounds like partial context leading to lower-quality outputs - we'll add recommendations for prompt-chunking or shorter seq lengths for those use cases.
[03:28] Maya Patel: Good. For the renewal we need hard SLAs on availability and incident response. What do you propose?
[03:33] Alexis Kim: For Dedicated we support a 99.95 SLA in our enterprise tiers. For hosted with reserved commitments we can offer operational playbooks and faster incident escalation.
[03:44] Samuel Ortiz: We also need clearer audit logs and HSM key handling - Elena will own review of the security artifacts.
[03:50] Elena Park: Yes we need KMS/HSM diagrams and table-level logging retention info. Also SSO integration details - we saw some mismatched roles when provisioning last month.
[03:59] Priya Nair: Noted - we'll share the SOC2 package, the ISO attestation, and HSM integration notes. There is also a private deployment blueprint if you want an on-prem option.
[04:10] Maya Patel: On that - timeline? We want private for EU data residency and some PHI flows.
[04:15] Priya Nair: Typical timeline for Private evaluation is 4-8 weeks for architecture & pilot, depending on your infra readiness. The first step is an architecture session to align on network, KMS, and NFS/ephemeral storage.
[04:28] Samuel Ortiz: Our infra team prefers VPC peering + customer-managed KMS. Can Redwood support HSM-in-cloud?
[04:33] Alexis Kim: Yes we have HSM integrations and can work with your vendor for key wraps; we'll include options in the artifact pack.
[04:40] Diego Martinez: Back to costs - Maya, one optimization is to quantize the model for batch scoring. That can drop GPU hours by ~40-60 for certain models. We ran a quick internal bench for a quantized LLM variant with similar output quality for scoring tasks.
[04:56] Maya Patel: How much engineering effort? We can't break things in prod.
[04:59] Priya Nair: For inference it's low. Redwood Optimize can recommend quantization profile and we can run a small pilot with a shadow copy of your scoring pipeline. It requires validation tests and evals - typical pilot 2 weeks.
[05:12] Jordan Lee: We'll take that pilot. Schedule it after the architecture session.
[05:16] Maya Patel: OK good. Anything on observability? Our team had lots of noisy alerts during the incident.
[05:21] Diego Martinez: We recommend tuning your alert thresholds to token-level latency percentiles and adding tracing hooks for retried requests; we'll also send a dashboard template that highlights cost by route, model, and token bucket.
[05:33] Alexis Kim: Quick question - competitors, you mentioned considering on-prem. What drove that?
[05:37] Samuel Ortiz: Regulatory concerns and a perception of cost control. Also the benching team saw better raw throughput with vendor X in some numbers but no platform-level ops.
[05:47] Priya Nair: Worth calling out that platform-level features - automatic KV cache, continuous batching, fallback - reduce ops overhead. We'll send a comparison sheet with measured latencies for your workload.
[05:58] Maya Patel: Good. Let's talk timeline for renewal - we want the legal review to start mid-March and commercial by end of March.
[06:05] Alexis Kim: Sounds doable. Diego will circulate pricing scenarios and term options this week.
[06:10] Diego Martinez: I'll aim to send by Monday.
[06:12] Maya Patel: Great. Any open questions?
[06:15] Elena Park: One security ask - can you provide a description of logging retention and log access controls per role?
[06:21] Priya Nair: Yes we'll add a RBAC doc with retention settings.
[06:25] Samuel Ortiz: Also, for the pilot, can we run sample throughput tests with our typical 5k requests per minute pattern? Need to ensure the KV cache warms.
[06:33] Priya Nair: Absolutely - include that in the pilot spec. We'll do a preflight to validate warm cache behavior.
[06:39] Maya Patel: OK let's do a recap. Diego?
[06:42] Diego Martinez: Recap - Redwood will: 1) send 90-day cost breakout and rightsizing suggestions (due 3/12), 2) send security artifacts SOC2/ISO/HSM notes and RBAC doc (due 3/09), 3) schedule architecture session for private pilot with Elena and Priya - target wk Mar 22, 4) run a 2-week quantized-model pilot after architecture signoff, 5) Alexis to send renewal pricing scenarios (due 3/09).
[07:10] Maya Patel: That matches our expectations. Any other items?
[07:14] Alexis Kim: No - thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the spreadsheet and calendar invites.
[07:18] Jordan Lee: Thanks.
[07:19] Samuel Ortiz: Thanks all.
[07:20] Elena Park: Bye.
[07:21] Diego Martinez: Bye.
[07:22] Priya Nair: End call.
